findings.title: Annual-aggregate thresholds are not modelled for §194J, §194H, §194A, §194D, §194G or §194Q — the engine silently deducts nothing on repeat vendors
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/tds/section_rates.py:110-150 gives only §194C an `aggregate_threshold_paise`; every other section is a bare `single_threshold_paise`. apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:304-307: `applies = taxable_paise > rule.single_threshold_paise or (rule.aggregate_threshold_paise is not None and fy_total > rule.aggregate_threshold_paise)` — with `aggregate_threshold_paise is None` for 194J/194H/194A/194D/194G/194Q the FY aggregate is never tested. Run in this session: `resolve_tds('194J', 45_000_00, fy_prior_taxable_paise=4_00_000_00, fy='2025-26')` → `applies=False, tds=0`; `resolve_tds('194H', 15_000_00, prior=1_00_000_00)` → 0; `resolve_tds('194Q', 10_00_000_00, prior=1_00_00_000_00)` → 0. §194J's own proviso reads 'the amount of such sum or, as the case may be, the AGGREGATE of the amounts of such sums credited or paid ... during the financial year does not exceed fifty thousand rupees'; §194H, §194A, §194D and §194G are worded the same way, and §194Q charges on purchases 'of the value or aggregate of such value exceeding fifty lakh rupees in any previous year'. The module docstring at section_rates.py:52-56 claims the modelling is 'CONSERVATIVE ... so the tool over-flags rather than silently under-deducts', which is the opposite of what the shape does.
findings.ca_experience: A consultant billed ₹40,000 in April, ₹40,000 in July and ₹40,000 in October under §194J: the platform withholds ZERO on all three, when ₹12,000 was due from the first bill's aggregate crossing. The CA discovers it at year end or when the assessing officer disallows 30% of the ₹1,20,000 under §40(a)(ia) and charges §201(1A) interest at 1%/month from each credit date. Same failure on every commission agent under §194H (₹20,000 FY aggregate) and on every §194Q buyer.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime, Zoho Books and Saral TDS all track the per-deductee per-section FY cumulative and trigger the deduction — and retrospectively deduct on the crossing bill — because that is the only way the proviso can be honoured. Tally's 'TDS Nature of Payment' master carries both the single and the exemption-limit figures.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `aggregate_threshold_paise` to every section whose proviso is an FY aggregate (194A 10_000_00, 194D/194G/194H 20_000_00, 194J 50_000_00, 194Q 50_00_000_00) and keep the single-payment figure only where the statute genuinely is per-payment (194C ₹30,000, 194I ₹50,000 per month, 194B per transaction). `_resolve_bill_resident_tds` already computes `fy_prior` for every section, so the plumbing exists. Decide and encode what happens on the crossing bill: the statute requires TDS on the whole aggregate, so the crossing bill must withhold on `fy_total`, not just on itself.

findings.title: §194Q withholds 0.1% of the whole invoice instead of 0.1% of the sum exceeding ₹50 lakh — a six-fold over-deduction
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:317: `tds = taxable_paise * rate_bps // 10000` applied to the full `taxable_paise` for every section including 194Q (`"194Q": TDSSectionRule(50_00_000_00, 10, 10)` at apps/api/domain/tds/section_rates.py:141). §194Q(1) charges 'a sum equal to 0.1 per cent of such sum EXCEEDING fifty lakh rupees'. Run in this session: `resolve_tds('194Q', 60_00_000_00, fy='2025-26')` → ₹6,000 withheld; the statute gives ₹1,000 (0.1% of ₹10 lakh).
findings.ca_experience: On a ₹60 lakh purchase the client withholds ₹6,000 instead of ₹1,000 and short-pays the supplier by ₹5,000. The supplier's 26AS shows a credit that does not match its books, and the buyer's 26Q reports a figure it cannot reconcile to §194Q. The error scales — on a ₹5 crore annual purchase the over-deduction is ~₹45,000.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime and Zoho Books both compute §194Q on the excess over the ₹50 lakh threshold and carry the running cumulative per supplier per FY; ClearTax's TDS module does the same. The identical 'on the excess' rule applies to TCS §206C(1H), which this codebase does not implement at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Give TDSSectionRule a `charges_on_excess: bool` (true for 194Q, and for 206C(1H) when TCS is built) and compute `max(0, fy_total - threshold) * rate_bps // 10000` less what has already been withheld this FY. Add the §194Q(1) proviso's ₹10-crore-turnover precondition on the buyer as a named gap rather than assuming it.

findings.title: "Prepare a Return" on /tds/returns cannot work in production — it sends no auth token, and the deductions it looks for carry a NULL financial_year and a differently-formatted quarter
findings.evidence: Three independent breaks on one path. (1) apps/web/lib/data/tds.ts:112-119 and :123-130 — `compute26Q`/`compute24Q` call `fetch(...)` with only `Content-Type`, no `Authorization`; apps/api/routers/tds.py:130 and :214 gate both on `Depends(rbac("tds","compute"))`, and apps/api/core/auth.py:171-175 raises 401 when the Bearer header is absent (the dev fallback at auth.py:153-169 applies only when SUPABASE_URL is unset). Every other call in the same file goes through `authedFetch` (lib/data/tds.ts:135-149). (2) apps/api/services/tds_register_service.py:218-252 — the upsert payload writes `quarter` but never `financial_year`; migration 263 added the column and nothing backfills new rows (apps/api/migrations/263_tds_deductions_financial_year.sql:44-75 backfills existing rows only, no trigger). (3) the register writes `quarter` as `"Q3 2025-26"` (tds_register_service.py:89-96, asserted in apps/api/tests/test_tds_register_follows_the_bill.py:196) while apps/web/app/tds/returns/page.tsx:104 calls `getTDSDeductions(clientId, financialYear, quarter)` with `quarter` of type `TDSQuarter = "Q1"|...` and lib/data/tds.ts:227-233 filters `.eq("financial_year", fy).eq("quarter", quarter)`.
findings.ca_experience: The CA picks a client, FY and quarter, clicks Compute, and gets "No TDS deductions found for this period. Add deductions from the TDS Deductions tab" — even when the client has fifty posted purchase bills with TDS. If they add rows by hand on /tds (which writes quarter as "Q1 (Apr-Jun)") the filter still misses, and if it ever matched, the POST would come back 401 Unauthorized as "26Q compute failed". The one screen labelled 'Prepare a Return' can never produce a return.
findings.market_standard: Saral TDS, Winman TDS and ClearTDS all assemble the quarter from the deduction register with no re-keying, and every one of them ships a working FVU output. This is the core task of a TDS module.
findings.suggested_fix: Switch compute26Q/compute24Q to the file's own `authedFetch`. Write `financial_year` in `sync_for_bill`'s upsert (fy_label(when) already exists in the module). Then delete the browser-side assembly entirely and point the screen at `POST /api/tds/26q/from-books` and `/24q/from-books`, which are already correct and already GL-reconciled — see TDS-05 and TDS-06 for what the browser path also gets wrong.

The screen therefore always reports 'No TDS deductions found'. findings.title: Form 16/16A certificate creation always fails silently against the real database — the UI sends "Form 16A", the CHECK constraint accepts only "16A"
findings.evidence: apps/api/migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:89: `certificate_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (certificate_type IN ('16','16A','16B','16C'))`; no later migration alters it (grep over migrations/*.sql for certificate_type returns only that line). apps/web/app/clients/[id]/compliance/tds/page.tsx:681 seeds the form with `certificate_type: "Form 16A"` and :739-744 offers `<option>Form 16</option><option>Form 16A</option>`. apps/api/routers/tds_workspace.py:561 writes `"certificate_type": body.certificate_type` verbatim. The handler's `except Exception` at tds_workspace.py:586-588 turns the constraint violation into `api_response(False, None, str(e))` — an HTTP 200 — and apps/web/app/clients/[id]/compliance/tds/page.tsx:702-707 (`saveNew`) never inspects the response, it just closes the panel and reloads. Every mock-mode test passes because `_USE_MOCK` writes a dict (tests/test_phase3_tds.py:111 uses "Form 16A"); the only real-Postgres insert, tests/test_gst_tds_schema_drift_pg.py:291, uses '16A'.
findings.ca_experience: The CA fills in the deductee, PAN, FY, section and amount, clicks 'Generate Draft', the panel closes — and the certificate list is unchanged. No error, no toast, nothing in the console the CA would see. They try again, and again. Form 16A tracking simply does not work on the deployed product.
findings.market_standard: Form 16A is generated on TRACES, but Saral TDS, ClearTDS and Winman all maintain the request/download/issue register and bulk-merge the TRACES PDFs per deductee. Here even the register row cannot be created.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise at the router — map 'Form 16'→'16', 'Form 16A'→'16A' — or change the select values. Then stop swallowing DB errors into a 200: `create_certificate` should raise 422 on a constraint violation, and `saveNew` must check `r.success` and surface `r.error`. Add a real-Postgres test that posts the request model the UI actually sends.

findings.title: The /tds page computes TDS in the browser from a hardcoded, stale rate table and writes it straight to tds_deductions, bypassing the engine and rbac()
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/tds/page.tsx:49-61 hardcodes `TDS_SECTIONS` with `194D: 5%` and `194H: 5%` — both cut to 2% by the Finance (No.2) Act 2024 from 01-10-2024, and correctly 200 bps in apps/api/domain/tds/section_rates.py:126,130. The file header (lines 3-16) also cites §194A '₹40,000 bank, ₹5,000 others', the pre-Finance-Act-2025 figures. app/tds/page.tsx:159-171 auto-fills the rate from that table and computes `const tdsPaise = Math.round((grossPaise * tdsRate) / 100)` — no threshold, no §194C aggregate, no §206AA no-PAN floor, and `Math.round` where the backend floors (`tds_computer.py:317` uses `// 10000`). :183-197 and :764-778 then `sb.from("tds_deductions").insert({...})` over PostgREST, so `rbac("tds","compute")` never runs and `TDSComputer.resolve_tds` is never called. CLAUDE.md: 'Zero business logic in the frontend'.
findings.ca_experience: A CA recording a ₹1,00,000 commission under §194H sees the rate auto-fill to 5% and ₹5,000 withheld. The correct figure is 2% / ₹2,000. They have over-deducted ₹3,000 from the payee, and the row lands in the register with `tds_rate_pct = 5.00` and goes onto the 26Q working paper at that rate. A ₹20,000 §194J payment gets 10% withheld even though it is below the ₹50,000 threshold.
findings.market_standard: Every one of Tally, Zoho Books, ClearTax and Saral holds one rate master, updates it by patch each Finance Act, and computes centrally. None of them lets a UI carry its own copy.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `TDS_SECTIONS` with a `listTdsSections(fy)` call (the endpoint exists — routers/tds.py:371, and apps/web/app/accounting/suppliers/page.tsx:186 already does exactly this) and the amount with `computeTdsAmount({section, payment_amount_paise, pan, fy})` (routers/tds.py:335). Move the insert behind a POST endpoint so rbac and the register's own rules apply. Add a lint/test that fails on any TDS rate literal under apps/web.

verification.what_is_actually_true: Confirmed, and the numbers are worse than a stale label: the page's 5% for §194D/§194H is double the engine's 2%, and the page deducts with no threshold at all where the engine refuses below one. Probed against the real registry — 194H on ₹1,00,000 gives ₹2,000 (2%) and 194J on ₹20,000 gives ₹0 (below_threshold), while apps/web/app/tds/page.tsx:159-171 would produce ₹5,000 and ₹2,000 respectively. The write is a raw PostgREST insert (page.tsx:183-197, :764-777) with only firm-scoped RLS behind it (migrations/014:196-198), and the repo's own unguarded-direct-write tracker misses the table entirely.

findings.title: On a 26Q working paper every deductee row is stamped with the first challan found for its section, and deposits are apportioned by weight rather than matched to the month
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:215: `matching_challan = next((c for c in challans if (c.get("section") or "") == section), None)` — the first challan in an unordered PostgREST result (`_deposited_challans` at :150-153 issues no `.order()`). A quarter always has three monthly deposits under Rule 30 (7 May, 7 Jun, 7 Jul for Q1), all carrying the same section, so all three months' deductees are labelled with whichever one comes back first. Separately, :200-209 apportions `min(deposited_total, sum(weights))` across the section's bills by largest-remainder, so a bill fully deposited in April is shown as partly deposited whenever the quarter as a whole is short.
findings.ca_experience: The CA downloads the Q1 26Q working paper to key into the RPU and finds every June deductee pointing at the April challan's BSR code and serial. The FVU cross-checks deductee rows against the challan they sit under, so the statement is rejected — or worse, accepted with the wrong challan and every one of those deductees' 26AS entries booked 'U' (unmatched), which the deductees then chase the client about. The 'deposited' column against each vendor is a proportion, not what was actually paid for that vendor.
findings.market_standard: In the NSDL RPU the deductee annexure is physically nested under its challan; Saral TDS, Winman and ClearTDS all require the deduction to be tagged to a specific challan, and refuse to build the file until every deduction is mapped. Tally's 'TDS Challan Reconciliation' does the same.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `challan_id` FK on `tds_deductions` (migration 037 already added `tds_return_id`; the challan link was the one it named and did not create) and a challan-mapping screen. Failing that, match a bill to the challan whose deposit period covers the bill's month — deduction month → deposit due 7th of the next month, March → 30 April — and order the challan query deterministically.

verification.what_is_actually_true: Confirmed. Every deductee row in a 26Q working paper is stamped with one challan per section (apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:215, :224-226) regardless of which of the quarter's three monthly deposits actually covered that bill, and tds_deposited_paise is a largest-remainder share of the section's total deposit (:200-209), not the amount deposited for that deductee. The only correction: the challan order is by UUID via _paginate_all's `.order("id")` (:74), not undefined — arbitrary with respect to month either way. No challan FK exists on tds_deductions (migrations/014:183-185; 037:41-45 names one and adds only tds_return_id).

lens_notes.literal: apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:215 is exactly `matching_challan = next((c for c in challans if (c.get("section") or "") == section), None)`, and every deductee row for a section takes that same challan's challan_no, bsr_code and payment_date (:224-226). One correction to the evidence: the challan list is not strictly unordered — _deposited_challans (:150-153) issues no .order(), but _paginate_all (:60-79) adds `.order(key)` with key="id", so 'first' is the lowest UUID. Deterministic, and still unrelated to the deposit month, which is the substance of the finding. The apportionment claim is also literal: :200-209 computes shares = apportion(min(deposited_total, sum(weights)), weights) over all of a section's bills, so a bill deposited in full in April is shown as part-deposited whenever the quarter's total deposit is short of the quarter's total deduction.
lens_notes.guards: None. tds_deductions has challan_no/challan_date/bsr_code as loose TEXT (apps/api/migrations/014_complete_missing_tables.sql:183-185) and no challan FK — migration 037's own comment at :41-42 says 'Add challan_id FK to existing tds_deductions table' and line :45 then adds only tds_return_id. findings.ca_experience: A client deducted ₹80,000 in June and deposited it on 20 August. The CA has to work out on paper that §201(1A)(ii) charges 1.5% per month or part from the DATE OF DEDUCTION (not the due date) — three part-months, ₹3,600 — and add it to the challan by hand under the right minor head. The platform neither warns that the deposit is late nor tells them the number. Same for the ₹200/day §234E fee, which must be paid before the statement can be filed at all.
findings.market_standard: Saral TDS, Winman TDS, ClearTDS and TaxCloud all compute §201(1A) interest per deduction from the deduction date and §234E from the Rule 31A due date, and print both onto the challan 281 worksheet. Tally Prime shows interest on its 'TDS Outstanding' report.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `domain/tds/interest.py` with two pure functions — `interest_201_1a(deducted_on, deposited_on, amount_paise, failure: 'not_deducted'|'not_deposited')` at 1%/1.5% per month or part, and `fee_234e(due_date, filed_on, tds_paise)` capped at the TDS — with unit tests, and surface both on the challan create screen and the return screen. Both are pure arithmetic over dates the system already holds.

findings.title: TCS (§206C(1H)/(1F)/(1G), Form 27EQ, Form 27D) does not exist — only a rate row nobody reads
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/tds/section_rates.py:142-149 carries `"206C": TDSSectionRule(0, 10, 10)` with its own comment: 'NOT wired to any computation anywhere in this codebase — confirmed zero readers ... do not assume TCS is an implemented feature because a rate exists here.' grep for 'tcs' in apps/api/routers/sales_invoices.py and routers/receipts.py returns nothing; the only other hits are the `TCS_RETURN` task-type enums in migrations/001, 002 and 006 and the `27EQ` label in domain/tds/vocabulary.py:96,100. `tds_returns.return_type` and `tds_deductions.return_type` both allow '27EQ' (migrations/037:13, 014:188) and nothing ever writes it.
findings.ca_experience: An SME client selling over ₹50 lakh to one buyer must collect 0.1% TCS under §206C(1H), show it on the invoice, deposit it, file 27EQ quarterly and issue Form 27D. None of that is possible here — the CA runs it in Tally or a spreadsheet, which is exactly the 'one platform' claim breaking. A client selling a motor vehicle over ₹10 lakh (§206C(1F)) or remitting under LRS (§206C(1G)) has the same problem.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime computes TCS on the invoice line and files 27EQ; Zoho Books supports 206C(1H); Saral and Winman both ship 27EQ and Form 27D. TCS is table stakes for any product claiming to replace Tally for a trading SME.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope it as its own build: a TCS nature master (1H/1F/1G/scrap/timber), collection on the sales invoice at the point of receipt (206C(1H) is collection-on-receipt, not on invoice), a `tcs_collections` register mirroring `tds_deductions`, the 27EQ statement, and Form 27D. Note that §206C(1H) charges on the receipt EXCEEDING ₹50 lakh — the same excess rule as TDS-02.

verification.what_is_actually_true: The code reading is confirmed — TCS is genuinely unimplemented end to end — but the finding's headline case is statutorily stale, and the repo's own research says so: docs/audits/2026-09-07-market-research/income-tax-tds-primary.md:564-582 records that §206C(1H) TCS on sale of goods CEASED TO OPERATE FROM 01-04-2025, with §194Q taking the ground. So 'an SME selling over ₹50 lakh to one buyer must collect 0.1% TCS' has been wrong for the whole of FY 2025-26, and the suggested fix should not build 206C(1H) collection. The live gap is §206C(1) (scrap, timber and the rest), §206C(1F) motor vehicles over ₹10 lakh and §206C(1G) LRS/overseas tour, plus Form 27EQ and Form 27D. Separately, the only TDS deposit obligation is `TDS_SALARY_DEPOSIT`, generated from payroll (`_payroll_obligations` at :307-315 with `_PAYROLL_OBLIGATION_TYPE` at :320-324); there is no monthly obligation for the vendor/26Q side, even though `compliance_engine.tds_deposit_due_date` (services/compliance_engine.py:292-306) computes the correct 7th-of-next-month / 30-April-for-March rule and would serve it unchanged.

findings.title: The 26AS parser mislabels Part B (TCS) as TDS and Part D (refunds) as self-assessment tax, and nothing filters non-TDS parts out before matching
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/income_tax/form26as_service.py:186-194: `mapping = {"A": "tds_salary", "B": "tds_other", "C": "advance_tax", "D": "self_assessment", "F": "tds_other"}`. In Form 26AS, Part B is TCS collected, Part C is tax paid other than TDS/TCS, Part D is DETAILS OF PAID REFUND, and Part F is TDS on sale of immovable property (buyer's view). Then `_entries_from_records` (:324-337) converts every parsed record into a `Form26ASEntry` with no filter on `part` or `record_type`, and `run_reconciliation` (:558-560) feeds all of them into `_m.reconcile`, whose totals (`total_26as_paise` at domain/income_tax/form26as_matcher.py:431) sum every entry.
findings.ca_experience: A CA pastes a full 26AS. The variance figure the whole screen is built around — and the AI insight it triggers (:454-464) — is wrong, and the CA chases credits that were never TDS.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax's 26AS/AIS import and TaxCloud both parse 26AS by part and keep TDS, TCS, advance tax, self-assessment tax and refunds in separate buckets, because they feed different schedules of the ITR.

Confidence is medium only because the 26AS part layout is quoted from knowledge, not from a specimen in this repo — verify against a real statement before changing the map.

findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/tds/section_195.py:105-121 chooses between exactly two ladders — `surcharge_foreign_company` (2% over ₹1 crore, 5% over ₹10 crore) and `surcharge_non_corporate` (10/15/25/37) — on the boolean `is_company`, which apps/api/routers/purchase_bills.py:376 derives from `is_company_pan(vendor.pan)`; that function (apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:131-141) returns True for every PAN whose 4th character is not P or H, so 'F' (firm/LLP) and 'A'/'B' (AOP/BOI) and co-operatives all land in the foreign-company branch. The same boolean also selects `company_rate_bps=3500` for `other_sums` (domain/tds/section_195_rates.py:173-176) instead of the 30% non-corporate rate. Part II of the First Schedule gives a firm or a co-operative society a single 12% surcharge above ₹1 crore, which is neither of the two ladders held.
findings.ca_experience: On a ₹2 crore payment to a foreign partnership for 'other sums', the surcharge applied is 2% (foreign-company band) instead of 12%, and the base rate 35% instead of 30% — two errors in opposite directions that do not cancel. findings.market_standard: Not a comparison point — no mass-market Indian product computes §195 well; this module is already ahead of them. The defect is internal.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `is_company` boolean with a payee-class enum derived from the PAN's 4th character (individual/HUF, firm/LLP, AOP/BOI, company, co-operative, trust) and hold one surcharge ladder per class, plus the correct 'other sums' rate per class. findings.title: tds_section_limits ships seeded with pre-Finance-Act-2025 thresholds and pre-2024 rates, and its aggregate §194C row is silently dropped

findings.ca_experience: Nothing today — nothing reads it. findings.market_standard: n/a — internal data hygiene.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the table in a migration, or add a comment on it pointing at `domain/tds/section_rates.py` as the authority and a test that asserts it has no readers. findings.title: The 26Q/24Q from-books flow makes the CA re-type the TAN, deductor name, PAN and address every quarter, and validates the TAN only by length

Yet migration 325 created `client_statutory_identity.tan` with a real format CHECK (`apps/api/migrations/325_a_client_has_its_own_statutory_registrations.sql:90`) precisely for this — its own header at :20 says 'The visible consequence is routers/tds.py: Compute24QRequest takes `tan`'. That table is read only by payroll (apps/api/routers/payroll.py:3609, :3698). Validation is weak too: `_validate_26q` (apps/api/domain/tds/tds_computer.py:331-332) checks `len(payload.tan) != 10` while `TDSValidator.validate_tan` with the real `^[A-Z]{4}[0-9]{5}[A-Z]$` regex (domain/tds/tds_validator.py:11, :21-23) is never called on it.
findings.ca_experience: Four fields re-typed per client per quarter per form — for a firm with forty clients that is 640 keystrokes of statutory identity a year, each of them an opportunity to key a wrong TAN that the length check will happily accept ('1234567890' passes). A wrong TAN on a filed statement is a correction statement.
findings.market_standard: Every TDS product holds the deductor master — TAN, name, address, responsible person, designation, PAN — once per client and never asks again. Saral and Winman also validate the TAN check-format on entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Default the four fields from `client_statutory_identity` (adding deductor address and responsible-person columns there if absent) and let the CA override. Call `TDSValidator.validate_tan` in `_validate_26q`/`_validate_24q` instead of the length check.

findings.title: Nothing computes what TDS is due for deposit this month, so there is no challan-281 worksheet to pay from
findings.evidence: `tds_deductions` rows carry `transaction_date` and `quarter` but no deposit-period grouping, and no endpoint aggregates them by deduction month. `POST /api/tds-workspace/challans` (apps/api/routers/tds_workspace.py:261-310) takes an amount the CA types in and books the whole of it as `tds_paise` with `total_paise` equal to it and `interest_paise`/`penalty_paise` left at their defaults; `minor_head` is fixed at '200' by the column default (apps/api/migrations/037_tds_engine.sql:72) with no way to record a 400 (regular assessment) deposit. `compliance_engine.tds_deposit_due_date` (apps/api/services/compliance_engine.py:292-306) computes the correct 7th/30-April rule and is called only from `payroll_deposit_due_dates`.
findings.ca_experience: On the 5th of the month the CA has to work out, per client and per section, how much TDS was deducted last month and is due by the 7th. The platform holds every deduction row and will not add them up for them. They export to Excel — the exact workflow the product exists to replace.

findings.title: Purchase debit and credit notes never reverse TDS, so a return after deduction leaves the register and the 26Q overstated
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:33-37 states it plainly: 'purchase debit/credit notes never adjust tds_paise in this codebase (confirmed — routers/debit_notes.py and routers/purchase_credit_notes.py never touch it), so a purchase return after TDS was already deducted and deposited is not modelled here either.' Confirmed: the 26Q builder reads only `purchase_bills` (`_posted_vendor_tds_bills` at :132-137) and no note table. `sync_for_bill` (apps/api/services/tds_register_service.py:128) is keyed on `purchase_bill_id` and has no note counterpart.
findings.ca_experience: A ₹5 lakh §194J bill is booked, ₹50,000 withheld and deposited. The vendor then issues a credit note for ₹2 lakh. The 26Q still reports a ₹5 lakh payment with ₹50,000 TDS, and the vendor's 26AS shows credit on income they did not earn. The CA has to adjust it outside the system, and the books-to-GL reconciliation on the return (:290-296) will still say 'matched' because the GL was never adjusted either.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime reverses the TDS on a purchase return through its 'TDS Adjustment' voucher and carries the adjustment into the quarterly return; Zoho Books nets the credit note against the deduction.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the policy first — a credit note in the same quarter reduces the deduction, one after deposit becomes an excess-deposit adjustment carried to the next quarter — then implement it in the register and the 26Q builder. It is an accounting decision as much as a coding one.

verification.what_is_actually_true: Purchase debit and credit notes carry no TDS handling at all — apps/api/routers/debit_notes.py and apps/api/routers/purchase_credit_notes.py contain no occurrence of 'tds' in any case — and the 26Q builder reads only posted purchase_bills with tds_paise > 0 (apps/api/services/tds_return_service.py:132-137), while the register syncs per purchase_bill_id only (apps/api/services/tds_register_service.py:128,:163,:218). A purchase return after deduction leaves both the register and the 26Q overstated, and the books-vs-GL reconciliation at :289-296 still reports 'matched' because neither side moved.

maturity.rationale: Two very different halves. The DOMAIN LAYER is among the strongest work in this repo: domain/tds/section_195.py asks chargeability before rate and cites GE India Technology Centre; residency.py transcribes the resident-only charging words from the Act rather than inferring them; vocabulary.py forks the 1961 and 2025 Acts by event date and refuses the s.393 payment codes rather than inventing them; form26as_matcher.py is a genuinely good four-pass identity-first reconciler that reports the Rule 37BA(1) direction most tools ignore; and 446 tests across sixteen TDS test modules pass. But the PIPELINE from that domain layer to a CA's desk is broken in several independent places at once. The core resident computation under-deducts on every repeat vendor because only §194C has an FY-aggregate threshold (TDS-01), and over-deducts six-fold on §194Q (TDS-02). The one screen called 'Prepare a Return' cannot produce a return in production — no auth header, NULL financial_year, mismatched quarter format (TDS-03). Form 16A creation always fails silently against the real database (TDS-04). The /tds screen computes TDS in the browser off a stale rate table and writes straight to the database past rbac (TDS-05, TDS-11). There is no 27Q builder, no TCS at all, no §201(1A) interest, no §234E fee, no §197 certificate, no FVU output and no correction statement. Grade C rather than D because the foundations that are hard to build are right and the things that are wrong are mostly fixable in days, and grade C rather than B because a CA using this today would compute wrong withholding on ordinary domestic vendors — the most common case, not the exotic one.
maturity.would_a_ca_buy_this_module_alone: No — a TDS product a CA buys is one that produces an FVU-ready statement, computes §201(1A) interest and §234E fee, handles §197 certificates and maps deductions to challans, and this does none of those while also under-deducting on any vendor billed repeatedly below the section threshold.

open_questions_for_owner: Do you want the /tds top-level screen (browser-computed TDS, unpersisted challans, stale rate table) fixed or deleted? The per-client /clients/[id]/compliance/tds screen already calls the real API for almost everything it does, and keeping two TDS screens is how the two rate tables diverged in the first place. Deleting it is the cheaper and safer answer, but it is the only screen with a CSV import of deductions.

Is the FVU/RPU text-file writer in scope? It is the single feature that decides whether a CA buys the TDS module alone, it is months of work per form per FY, and everything else on this list is comparatively cheap. If it is not in scope, the honest positioning of this module is 'computes and reconciles TDS; you file in the free NSDL RPU' — which is defensible but should be said out loud on the screen.

Is TCS in or out? Section 206C(1H) affects any trading client with a buyer over ₹50 lakh, which is a large share of the SME book the platform targets, and it is entirely absent. It is a distinct build (collection on receipt, 27EQ, Form 27D), not a data-registry gap.

How should the §194J/§194H/§194A crossing bill behave once aggregate thresholds are modelled? The statute requires TDS on the whole aggregate once it is crossed, which means the crossing bill withholds more than its own 10% — that is correct but surprising, and it changes the vendor's net payable. Does that need a CA confirmation step, or should it just happen?

Do you want §197 lower-deduction certificates as a first-class master (number, rate, validity, ceiling, consumption tracking) or is honouring vendors.tds_rate_bps as a manual override enough for now? The current state — a rate the CA can type that the engine ignores — is the worst of the three.

The §195 rate registry is verified=False for every year and the resident registry is unverified for FY 2026-27, while today is 07-09-2026 and FY 2026-27 is live. Who is doing the Finance Act line-by-line confirmation, and by when? The fallback returns last year's figures confidently, which is the trap CLAUDE.md already names.

The tds_deductions register is written by two independent paths (the purchase-bill sync, and the browser) with different quarter formats and different completeness. Should the register become bill-only, with manual deductions entered as a document, or does it need to stay a free-standing register for TDS on rent, interest and journal-only payments that never reach a purchase bill? That decision determines whether the from-books 26Q builder or the register-based one is the right foundation.
strengths: domain/tds/section_195.py asks the questions in the statutorily correct ORDER — chargeability, then nature, then treaty, then PAN, then surcharge and cess — and refuses rather than guessing on the three that matter (no nature recorded, business profits with no no-PE declaration, a TRC on file with no treaty rate). It cites GE India Technology Centre (P) Ltd v. CIT (2010) 327 ITR 456 at :6-12 for why an ordinary import withholds nil rather than 20%. Nothing else in the Indian mass market gets this right.

domain/tds/residency.py:159-175 transcribes the 'to a resident' charging words of each of the twelve resident-only sections from the Act itself, and lists §194B separately at :181 because it charges 'to any person' — so the classification can be checked without leaving the file, and a future §194E is classified by reading rather than by pattern-matching. The refusal at :271-306 stops a resident section being recorded against a non-resident payee.

domain/tds/vocabulary.py forks the 1961 and 2025 Acts by EVENT date rather than migrating (:19-29), refuses to name a form without a period (:358-364), refuses the reverse s.393(1)→194-series map because it would have to invent one (:254-272), and refuses the sixty-seven s.393 payment codes outright (:282-301) rather than guessing them. Both vocabularies are permanent, which is correct — a belated FY 2025-26 return is Form 24Q for ever.

domain/income_tax/form26as_matcher.py:312-433 is a well-built reconciler: four passes strongest-identity-first (TAN+amount, name+amount, TAN, name), each consuming the credits it matches so no book credit is claimed twice, deterministic tie-breaking by date proximity, and — the part most tools miss — it reports the books→26AS direction and names it under Rule 37BA(1) as credit that is not claimable until the deductor corrects. TRACES booking status is honoured, with a blank status treated as NOT final (:121-130).

domain/payroll/form24q.py applies the 2025-Act vocabulary at the LINE level, not just the header (:164-165), and its challan filter deliberately accepts both the old and the new section label (:172-180) because 'a challan records what somebody typed, not which Act governs the quarter'. Its CSV working paper writes the missing payment-code gap and every readiness problem INTO the file (:315-330), so a downloaded document outlives the toast that warned about it.

services/tds_return_service.py reconciles the computed 26Q/24Q total to the GL 'TDS Payable' control account through the SPECIFIC journal entries the source documents posted rather than a date-range scan (:108-129, with the reasoning at :16-23), resolves the account by exact name to avoid the 'TDS Payable' / 'TDS Payable - Salary' substring ambiguity (:82-105), and pages every query with keyset paging so a client over 1,000 rows is not silently truncated (:60-79).

The TDS base is the taxable amount excluding GST by construction, not by a separate rule: purchase_bills passes `total_taxable` into resolve_tds and the register writes `taxable_amount_paise` (services/tds_register_service.py:230 with the CBDT Circular 23/2017 citation at :31-35), so the book and the return agree because they read the same number.

The DTAA table is modelled as a firm-level (country, nature) reading rather than a per-vendor field (services/treaty_rate_service.py:278-289 explains why the vendor column was wrong), ships empty and is never seeded, treats 'no article' as an ANSWER rather than a missing rate, and REFUSES rather than falling back to the Act rate when a TRC is on file with no rate recorded. The settings screen (apps/web/app/settings/treaty-rates/page.tsx) is reachable from Settings, validates one-thing-per-row server-side, and carries zero business logic.

apps/web/app/accounting/suppliers/page.tsx is the model the rest of the frontend should follow — it loads the section list from GET /api/tds/sections (:186) and computes the amount via POST /api/tds/compute-amount passing the PAN so is_company and §206AA are derived server-side (:135-145), rather than hardcoding anything.

446 tests pass across sixteen TDS-related modules (run in this session), including a bill-level engine test that proves the individual-vs-company rate split by PAN 4th character, a vendor-residency/27Q test, a register-follows-the-bill test that asserts a cancelled bill loses its row, and a real-Postgres upsert test.

§206AA is enforced on the ACTUAL withheld amount, not merely as a post-hoc warning (domain/tds/tds_computer.py:309-310, wired from routers/purchase_bills.py:340-343), and the §206AA(7)/Rule 37BC non-resident carve-out that residents do not get is implemented and gated on the six particulars actually being held (domain/tds/section_195.py:234-245, routers/purchase_bills.py:385-393).

Every threshold and rate lookup is keyed on the FY the BILL falls in, not today (routers/purchase_bills.py:324-337, :399-408), so a bill entered late for a prior year uses that year's law — and the response carries `rates_verified` so a firm can see when it is withholding on carried-forward figures (routers/tds.py:352-368, plus a dedicated /rate-coverage endpoint at :393).
subsystem: TDS/TCS — section rates and thresholds, TDS computer and validator, §195/DTAA/residency, the 1961-vs-2025 Act vocabulary fork, the deduction register and challans, 24Q/26Q/27Q preparation, Form 26AS matching, the TDS workspace, lower-deduction certificates, §201(1A) interest, §234E late fee and §206C TCS
test_coverage_notes: 446 tests pass across the sixteen TDS-facing test modules (test_tds_engine, test_tds_section_rates, test_section_195_rates, test_the_tds_vocabulary_carries_both_acts, test_tds_bill_engine, test_vendor_residency_and_27q, test_tds_register_follows_the_bill, test_form26as_reconciliation, test_dtaa_treaty_rates, test_tds_filing_pipeline, test_tds_return_reconciliation, test_tds_calculator_endpoint, test_phase3_tds, test_tds_repository, test_tds_client_scope, test_filing_demo_tds), verified by running them in this session. What is well covered: the §195 decision order and its refusals; the vocabulary fork in both directions with its two deliberate refusals; the per-bill individual-vs-company rate split by PAN 4th character; the register's create/update/remove lifecycle across bill status transitions; the 26AS matcher's four passes and one-to-one consumption; client-assignment scope on every TDS route. What is NOT covered, and where the bugs live: (1) no test exercises an FY aggregate for any section but §194C, which is why TDS-01 survives — test_tds_section_rates asserts thresholds exist and are non-negative, never that a second bill crossing the annual limit deducts; (2) no test asserts §194Q computes on the excess (TDS-02); (3) nothing tests that sync_for_bill writes financial_year, so TDS-03's NULL column is invisible; (4) every certificate test uses mock mode with 'Form 16A', while the single real-Postgres insert uses '16A' — the constraint mismatch of TDS-04 falls exactly in the gap between them (tests/test_phase3_tds.py:111 vs tests/test_gst_tds_schema_drift_pg.py:291); (5) there is no test of any apps/web TDS screen at all — no test would notice that compute26Q sends no Authorization header, that the challan modal never persists, or that the certificates tab reads columns that do not exist; (6) the one test written to catch unguarded direct writes (tests/test_direct_write_tables_are_role_guarded.py) has a regex whose 400-character tail cap makes it miss both tds_deductions inserts and the tds_returns upsert — I reproduced this by running the module's own _direct_write_tables(), which returns 21 tables and no tds_* table while '.insert(' appears twice in app/tds/page.tsx. One test asserts a statutory behaviour that is no longer law: tests/test_tds_engine.py:327-338 pins §206AB's doubled non-filer rate, omitted by the Finance Act 2025 from 01-04-2025 (see TDS-24; medium confidence on the omission, high confidence that the function is FY-blind and unwired). No test covers §201(1A), §234E, TCS, 27Q assembly or challan-to-deduction mapping, because none of those exist.
what_exists:
Backend. domain/tds/ holds six modules. section_rates.py is an FY-versioned registry (FY 2025-26 verified against the Finance Act 2025, FY 2026-27 carried forward) of fifteen sections in integer basis points, plus quarter_dates() deriving Rule 31A period and due dates from any FY label. tds_computer.py is the single resolution point: resolve_tds() applies the threshold, the individual-vs-company rate by PAN 4th character and the §206AA no-PAN floor, and builds 24Q/26Q payload objects with validation errors and warnings. tds_validator.py holds PAN/TAN regexes and §206AA/§206AB rate helpers. residency.py routes a deduction to 26Q or 27Q under Rule 31A(4), lists the resident-only charging sections verbatim, and defines six named statutory gaps with CA-readable messages. section_195.py and section_195_rates.py compute withholding on a payment to a non-resident by nature of income under s.115A and Part II of the First Schedule, apply §90(2) against a recorded treaty rate, add surcharge and cess, honour the §206AA(7)/Rule 37BC carve-out, and refuse in three defined cases. vocabulary.py forks the 1961 and 2025 Act form and section names by event date (24Q→138, 26Q→140, 27Q→144, 27EQ→143, 192→392, 194-series→393(1), 195→393(2), 206C→394, Form 16→130, 16A→131, 26AS→168, 15G/15H→121) and names the s.393 payment-code table as an unheld gap.

Routers: /api/tds (26q and 24q compute from a caller payload, 26q and 24q from-books, compute-amount, sections, rate-coverage, returns and deductions listings, and CRUD for the firm's DTAA treaty rates); /api/tds-workspace (dashboard, deductions, challans, returns with a status ladder pending→prepared→ca_approved→filed gated on an explicit CA confirmation, a PRN and Manager+, certificates, and a deductor-side 26AS comparison); /api/form-26as (upload, parse from pasted text, list, reconcile, get).
